factors.name: Size and branching volume
factors.summary: Very high loadings (0.92–0.97) of Size, Token split, Control flow complexity, Number of empty sequence flows and Coefficient of network connectivity, plus Maximum connector degree (0.80) and a moderate Connector Mismatch (0.56), describe larger nets with more splits, parallelism and arcs per node. Density loads moderately negatively (-0.43), consistent with density falling as nets grow. This factor explains about 50% of the variance.

factors.name: Connector degree and density
factors.summary: Average connector degree (0.90) and Density (0.81) load highly, so the factor captures nets whose connectors carry many arcs relative to net size. Connector Heterogeneity loads negatively (-0.49), suggesting such nets tend to use one connector type, and Maximum connector degree cross-loads moderately (0.41) beside its main loading on Factor 1.

factors.name: Sequential, separable structure
factors.summary: Separability (0.93) and Sequentiality (0.76) load highly, describing nets with many non-connector arcs and many nodes that are not articulation points. The factor is clear but rests on only two measures (about 15% of the variance).

factors.name: Connector type mix (weak)
factors.summary: Only Connector Heterogeneity loads notably (0.62), and it cross-loads on Factor 2 (-0.49). The factor explains only 4.4% of the variance, has an eigenvalue of 0.68, which is below 1, and goes beyond the suggested three factors, so it is likely a specific factor rather than a shared dimension.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for a factor analysis: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO is 0.83. The four varimax factors explain 86% of the variance. A dominant size and branching factor is accompanied by a connector degree and density factor and by a sequentiality and separability factor. The fourth factor is weak, being retained beyond the suggested three, and is carried only by Connector Heterogeneity. All measures are assigned, and the only formal cross-loading is Connector Heterogeneity.
caveats: Four factors were extracted although three were suggested, and the fourth factor (eigenvalue 0.68, 4.4% of the variance) is essentially a single-measure factor.
Connector Heterogeneity cross-loads on Factors 4 and 2, and Maximum connector degree and Density also load secondarily on other factors.
Connector Mismatch has a low communality (0.37), so it is only partly explained by the solution.
Connector Heterogeneity, Average connector degree and Density have MSA values just above 0.6.
Number of duplicate tasks was constant and removed, so it is not represented.
The results reflect shared variance in these 288 discovered nets and depend on the discovery algorithms, the rotation and the factor count, not on causal relations.
